caption:
Trump says US tech companies that build AI data centers in other countries will face a "tremendous tax."
He gave no details and said he had not told his own officials yet.
At home, he told towns to make data center builders pay them instead of shutting the projects down.

Should AI companies be forced to build their data centers in the US?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters, AP · Photo: Shelby Tauber/Reuters

paragraphs.text: President Donald Trump said on Friday, November 20, 2026, that American companies that build data centers outside the United States will be penalized, according to Reuters and the Associated Press. Speaking at a White House news conference after returning from a trip to Asia, he said such companies would face a "tremendous tax."

"We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," Trump said, according to Reuters. Reuters reported that the stated aim of the penalty is to help the American AI sector compete with Chinese rivals.

Trump did not describe how the tax would work, how large it would be or which companies it would cover. The Associated Press reported that he said he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan. Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were in the briefing room as he spoke, according to the AP.

Reuters named Equinix and Digital Realty as major American data center developers that build and operate facilities outside the United States. The news agency noted that developers often place data centers close to their users to reduce delays for time sensitive tasks such as payment processing, and that moving large volumes of data over long distances adds cost. A penalty on overseas sites could therefore complicate the global AI buildout, Reuters wrote.

The remarks followed other steps by the administration aimed at China. Reuters reported that the Commerce Department moved on Monday, November 16, to restrict exports of advanced AI chips to several Southeast Asian countries. According to Reuters, Chinese companies have kept access to advanced chips by renting computing capacity at data centers in countries that are allowed to import them. The AP reported that the administration also issued new rules that week restricting remote access to advanced US computing chips and servers.

Trump has been a strong supporter of building data centers in the United States, a position Reuters described as unpopular with voters. Local opposition has focused on electricity demand, utility costs and other effects on nearby communities. At the briefing, Trump urged Americans to accept construction while extracting concessions from developers. "Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but don't shut them off," he said, according to the AP. "We want them to build it here," he added.

The AP reported that the Senate approved bipartisan permitting legislation on Thursday, November 19, that would shorten timelines for energy projects and require data centers to pay for their energy use and for transmission upgrades. The bill now goes to the House. Trump praised the measure, saying it would cause "tremendous amounts of new building." The AP also reported that officials at Google and Meta said they are trying to address community mistrust with more transparency.

The comments point in two directions at once. The White House wants more AI computing built on American soil and less of it available to Chinese firms through foreign facilities, but the industry that would have to move that capacity home is already facing local resistance over power and prices. Without a written proposal, companies have little to plan around beyond the president's words.
Watch whether the administration or Congress turns the threat into a formal proposal, and whether large developers with overseas campuses respond by changing or pausing their building plans.
